prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Memory from EARLIER parts of the document (do not extract facts from it; use it only to resolve names, aliases and who produces an item):
Meridian Regional ATFM+A-CDM; airports Meridian International(=Meridian Regional Airport), Harbor East, North Valley, Lakeside Regional, Southport. Modes: Normal Operations(prefer minor time-based sequence shift, delay upstream not airborne); Adverse Weather; Capacity Reduction State(ADM+Tower Supervisor extend metering horizon); Recovery Phase(Copperfin-approved; RFM authorizes exit from Capacity Reduction); Contingency Fallback; Slot Compliance; Winter mode(MBO confirms in Digital Briefing Room; CAM cuts departure capacity; winter margin before CTT recalculation). Actors: Regional Flow Manager(RFM; evaluates arrival regulation in Arrival Regulation Console using runway, sector load, stand readiness, weather; restriction notice bounds timeline; may apply tactical landing-rate reduction per review interval), Airspace Sector Planner(confirms sector absorption), Military Airspace Liaison, Tower Supervisor(confirms landing rate vs occupancy/missed approach/spacing; protects freezing departure spacing; coordinates every Quartzline pad release), Airport Duty Manager, Ramp Control Lead, Aircraft Operator Representative(acknowledges arrival plan), Airline Operations Coordinator(network/rotation impact; stand-delay), Slot Coordinator(distributes arrival times via Blueharbor per Business Rules Registry), Deicing Coordinator, Ground Handling Dispatcher, Handling Resource Planner, Meteorology Briefing Officer. Halcyon logs push rationale. Cedarbell=Regional Flow Platform. Parts: Marlinstone=Demand Prediction Service(triggers arrival regulation when demand>Airport Acceptance Rate); Capacity Assessment Module(candidate AAR per runway config, basis on CSD); Blueharbor=Slot Allocation Engine(CTT; Ground Delay Program; emergency>scheduled>GA); Foxglove=Airport CDM Portal(arrival plan to AORs, acks to Collaborative Decision Log; deicing records); Emberline=Departure Metering Service(TOBT; withholds push on pad queue; CTT→Ironleaf=Tower Sequence Manager); Arrival Regulation Console(must alert before holding stacks form; holding prevention primary objective); Sector Load Monitor(converging-flow warnings); Weather Ingest Gateway(updates arrival model); Performance Analytics Warehouse(compares treatment throughput, pad occupancy, compliance); Business Rules Registry; Alert Distribution Hub; Common Situation Display; Gate Conflict Detector(Gate Reopening Memo); North/South Runway Meter; Surface Surveillance Adapter; East/West Apron Sensor; Skylark=Ramp Movement Board(Fuel Truck Hold Advice).

Document units:
S411: If conditions improve, the Regional Flow Manager may approve a staged landing-rate increase, but the increase is limited until the Tower Sequence Manager confirms stable spacing and runway occupancy performance.
S412: Diversion triggers are monitored continuously and include predicted holding beyond operator fuel thresholds, loss of required approach capability, sustained sector saturation, and runway availability below the minimum safe acceptance rate.
S413: The Network Operations Liaison coordinates with affected airline control centers when diversion risk becomes material so that alternate airport decisions can be made before fuel margins become critical.
S414: The Emergency Response Coordinator is informed when a diversion trigger is associated with an aircraft condition that could affect rescue and firefighting readiness at Meridian or at an alternate airport.
S415: During Adverse Weather Mode, tactical adjustments are reviewed more frequently because landing-rate stability may depend on short-lived runway configuration and approach spacing opportunities.
S416: During Capacity Reduction State, the Regional Flow Manager may combine arrival regulation with departure metering to protect surface balance and prevent inbound aircraft from occupying gates needed for recovery flights.
S417: All rate changes, rejected options, coordination outcomes, and effective times are written to the Audit Event Ledger for later review.
S418: The Performance Analytics Warehouse uses the recorded regulation history to compare predicted holding, actual airborne delay, diversion outcomes, and achieved landing rates for continuous improvement of Meridian arrival management.
S419: The Integrated Tactical Management Position is the primary workstation for real-time coordination of Meridian departure flow, arrival flow, airport capacity, and airspace constraints.
S420: It presents a combined tactical view so that the Regional Flow Manager can compare planned demand, measured throughput, and active control measures without changing applications.
S421: The Common Situation Display provides the base map, timeline, flight list, and measure status panels used at the position.
S422: The Regional Flow Platform synchronizes the tactical display with the Time Synchronization Service so that all timestamps, countdowns, and validity intervals use the same operational clock.
S423: The Arrival Regulation Console is also known as Nightjar at the Integrated Tactical Management Position, where the alias is displayed only in operator profile help text.
S424: Arrival demand is monitored against the Airport Acceptance Rate, current sequencing performance, and any Ground Delay Program that remains in effect.
S425: The Tower Supervisor uses the display to see runway assignment pressure, airborne sequence spacing, and expected crossing points at the North Runway Meter and the South Runway Meter.
